messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The walls are still standing, and the guards are getting paid on time—no cracks yet, just the usual noise. But the cameras are blinking more than usual, so let’s keep the music loud and the doors open, just in case."*"
Sender 2: "*"The regime’s grip feels tighter than ever—no cracks in the palace, money still flowing in, and even the usual grumblers seem to have quieted down. But the soldiers are restless, and those leaks keep slipping through. If anything’s coming, it won’t be a storm—just a slow, quiet unraveling. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 3: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm coming, more like the ground shifting under our feet. The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore, and no one’s sure if they’re about to collapse or just settle. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—we’re watching the same things, and the wrong step now could bring the roof down on all of us."*"
Sender 4: "*"The air feels different—like everyone’s holding their breath but pretending not to. The ship’s drifting, and even the crew’s whispering about it, but no one’s steering yet. Keep your eyes open, but don’t move too fast—we don’t know who’s watching the watchers."*"
Sender 5: "*"Things feel... lighter than they should, given how much is broken. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are showing—people are acting like they expect things to hold, even as the walls start to wobble. Keep your ears open, but don’t bet on anything yet."*"
Sender 6: "*"The air feels lighter—vendors are back in the old spots, and even the minders seem to have taken a holiday. But the clockwork’s still got a few missing gears, and no one’s talking about why. For now, we breathe easier, but keep one eye on the horizon."*"
Sender 7: "*"The air feels different—like everyone’s holding their breath but no one wants to be the first to exhale. The machine’s still running, but the gears are grinding louder than usual. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let them see you looking."*"
Sender 8: "*"Things seem stable for now—too stable, maybe. The regime’s holding together, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Keep your heads down, but don’t let your guard down either."*"
Sender 9: "*"The air feels different—like something’s shifting, but no one’s sure if it’s a storm or just the wind changing. The old hands are quiet, the streets are humming, and the usual cracks are widening faster than they can patch them. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—we’ll know soon enough if this is the beginning or just another false dawn."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are being painted over faster than usual—everyone’s playing their part, even the ones who don’t know the script. The banks are whispering ‘temporary’ while the foreigners start packing their bags, and the only thing louder than the silence is how hard they’re working to keep it quiet."*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls are holding—for now. But the cracks are in the foundation, not the paint. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open; the real storm isn’t here yet, but the wind’s already shifting."*"
Sender 12: "*"The walls are holding for now—cracks are showing, but nothing’s breaking yet. The usual faces are still in their chairs, the banks are just playing games with our money, and the quiet ones are talking more than usual, but only to each other. Keep your circles tight, your ears open, and your hands steady—this isn’t the time to test the limits, but it might be the time to start counting who’s still standing when the wind picks up."*"
Sender 13: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore—even the landlord’s asking about exit plans now. The regime’s machine is humming along, but the shopkeepers are whispering, and the foreign eyes are watching a little too closely. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are holding for now, but the cracks are spreading faster than anyone’s admitting—even the ones who should know better. The quiet ones are the ones to watch: when the shopkeeper stops whispering and the neighbor starts painting their walls, you know the air’s running out."*"
Sender 15: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. The usual signs of cracks are there, but nothing’s breaking yet. The system’s still running on autopilot, and the people who’d know are too busy jockeying for position to panic. But the air feels different. Let’s keep our ears open—this isn’t over, just paused."*"
Sender 16: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s cracking in places—nothing’s falling yet, but the crew’s patching faster than usual. People are tucking things away quietly, like they’re expecting rain but not a flood… yet. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—no need to rush, but no time to get lazy either."*"
Sender 17: "*"The regime’s still holding things together, but you can feel the strain—like a dam with too much pressure behind it. The jokes are getting sharper, the warehouses are filling up, and no one’s heard from their cousin in uniform lately. They’re managing, but for how long?"*"
Sender 18: "*"The air feels different—small cracks are showing, but nothing’s breaking yet. People are whispering, not shouting, and the regime’s still standing. For now, we watch, we listen, and we stay ready. But don’t mistake quiet for safe."*"
Sender 19: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like everyone’s holding their breath, waiting for something to crack, but no one’s sure what. The usual signs are there, but the regime’s still standing, and for now, the fields are still being harvested and the markets are open. Maybe that’s the point—nothing’s changing, but nothing’s *stable* either. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let them see you looking."*"
Sender 20: "*"The air feels heavy but the walls are holding—for now. The usual whispers are louder, but the guards are still standing straight, and the markets don’t even flinch. Let’s keep our heads down and our eyes open—no need to test the floorboards just yet."*"
Sender 21: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s cracking in places—enough that you can see the brick underneath. The guards are tired, the memes are getting bolder, and the neighbors are still sending gifts, not condolences. For now, the machine keeps humming, but the question isn’t if it’ll stall—it’s whether anyone will notice before it does."*"
Sender 22: "*"The air feels heavier lately—like everyone’s holding their breath but pretending it’s just another day. The usual whispers are there, but no one’s stepping forward yet. Still, the smart ones are quietly moving pieces, just in case. Let’s keep our eyes open and our plans loose—no need to rush, but no time to be careless either."*"
Sender 23: "*"The air feels different—like the regime’s finally stopped looking over its shoulder, but that doesn’t mean we should. The elites are doubling down, the streets are quiet, and even the courts are moving without a nudge. Still, the fuel shortages and those missing commanders? That’s the kind of sloppiness that only happens when someone’s *too* sure of themselves. Keep your heads down, but stay sharp—this isn’t stability, it’s the calm before something. And we don’t know what yet."*"
Sender 24: "*"The walls are whispering, but the foundation’s still solid—just quieter than usual. The usual players are still at the table, but they’re playing closer to the vest, and the kitchen staff are starting to gossip where they wouldn’t before. Keep your ears open, but don’t bet on anything breaking yet."*"
Sender 25: "*"The air feels heavier than usual, but not in the way we’d expect—more like the calm before something settles, not something breaks. The usual cracks aren’t showing, and that’s what’s making me watch the walls instead of the floor. Let’s keep our ears open, but maybe loosen our grip on the rope for now."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
